cohort: Live birth babies born in the last 12 months in rural Gedeo, Southern Ethiopia.
finding: The risk of neonatal death was higher for infants whose mothers did not attend antenatal care, gave birth by assisted or cesarean delivery, had some form of illness during pregnancy, were of very low birth weight, or were born prematurely, while maternal formal education was found to be protective.
mod_finding: Infants whose mothers gave birth by assisted or cesarean delivery had a higher risk of mortality.
